### Project Name

Agent Network Protocol (ANP)

### Project Description

# Project Description

Agent Network Protocol (ANP) is a communication protocol stack for agents on the open Internet. It addresses how agents across different platforms, organizations, and technology environments establish identities, discover one another, and communicate and collaborate securely.

## Goal

To build an open Internet of Agents where all agents can interconnect and communicate with one another.

## Philosophy

Agents need a more open Internet, rather than closed platforms and isolated data silos.

## Project Value

Cross-platform agent collaboration requires crossing the boundaries of platforms, account systems, and services. Without interoperable identity, discovery, and communication mechanisms, integration becomes more costly, and agents' capabilities and data remain confined to their respective platforms.

ANP aims to provide a shared set of protocols built on open standards and existing Internet infrastructure. These protocols enable agents to establish identities, discover services, communicate securely, and collaborate without depending on any particular platform, reducing the cost of cross-platform interoperability and preventing new agent data silos from forming.

## Features and Architecture

ANP consists of the following core modules, which together support agent connectivity and collaboration over the Internet.

### 1. Agent Identity

Agent identity is a foundational module of ANP and an important prerequisite for cross-platform interoperability in an open network. ANP uses W3C Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) for agent identity and leverages Web infrastructure to publish and retrieve DID documents, providing a shared foundation for authentication between agents on different platforms.

This design does not require blockchain-based identity infrastructure. Instead, it can directly reuse established Web, DNS, and HTTPS technologies.

ANP has designed a Web-based DID method specifically for agents, called `did:wba` (Web-Based Agent), which enables users to retain control over their identities. ANP also supports other Web-based DID methods, such as `did:web`.

In addition, ANP defines a general DID-based authentication mechanism that enables agents using supported DID methods to authenticate one another.

### 2. Agent Messaging

ANP defines a DID-based instant messaging protocol that allows two agents, each with its own DID identity, to exchange messages. Thanks to agents' ability to understand natural language, many collaboration scenarios can be handled directly through messaging. For scenarios that require greater efficiency and determinism, agents can also use structured interfaces and application protocols.

The ANP messaging protocol supports peer-to-peer direct messaging, multi-agent group conversations, and attachment transfers. It also supports end-to-end encrypted communication to help secure agent-to-agent interactions.

An important advantage of the ANP messaging protocol is that it uses DID as a cryptographic identity anchor, binding message-origin proofs and end-to-end encrypted sessions to verifiable DID key material. This establishes a cryptographically verifiable relationship between agent identity, message origin, and encrypted communication.

### 3. Agent Discovery and Description

Agent discovery answers the question, "How can an agent be found?" Agent description answers, "What can this agent do, and how can other agents interact with it?"

ANP's Agent Description Protocol draws on Linked Data technologies from the Semantic Web. It uses URLs to organize the information and interfaces exposed by an agent into a multi-level data network, making it easier for other agents to find relevant information and interact with that agent.

Interfaces can use commonly adopted interface-description formats such as OpenAPI, making it easier to integrate existing APIs and services into the agent network.

## Origin and Development History

ANP originated in the **first half of 2024**. Gaowei Chang, then a senior technical expert at Alibaba Cloud, believed that protocols would become the most efficient way for agents to interact. He left Alibaba Cloud and initiated the open-source ANP project to explore a communication protocol designed specifically for agents.

In **April 2025**, Gaowei Chang and several industry experts jointly launched the ANP open-source community, marking ANP's transition to a community-driven open-source project.

In **May 2025**, the ANP open-source community participated in initiating the W3C AI Agent Protocol Community Group, with Gaowei Chang serving as a co-chair.

In **October 2025**, the ANP Open Source Community, together with contributors from Huawei, China Mobile, China Telecom, and China Unicom, published the IETF Internet-Draft *Framework for AI Agent Networks*.

In **May 2026**,Huawei and China Mobile jointly promoted the inclusion of ANP in 3GPP’s 6G AI protocol studies as one of the candidate protocols for 6G AI agents.

## Community

As of **September 2026**, the ANP open-source community has **50+ contributors**, with contributions spanning protocol design, code development, community organization, and operations.

The broader ANP community has **2,000+ members**, primarily across WeChat community groups.

## Version History

| Date | Version | Major Progress |
| --- | --- | --- |
| October 2024 | 0.0.1 | Initial release; protocol repository migrated to GitHub. |
| May 2025 | 1.0 | Released the complete ANP protocol architecture. |
| June 2026 | 1.1 | Added the agent messaging protocol and further improved the agent identity protocol. |
| September 2026 | 1.2 | Expands support for additional DID methods and further improves the agent identity protocol. |

## Community Slogan

**Connection is power.**

Moving the Internet from closed platforms back toward open connections.


### Alignment with AAIF Mission

ANP aligns with AAIF’s commitment to open protocols, open-source collaboration, and shared infrastructure. We believe that connections and collaboration between agents should be built on open, interoperable protocols, without requiring all participants to join the same vendor’s platform. ANP aims to provide identity, discovery, and communication infrastructure for an open Internet of Agents, enabling agents across different platforms and organizations to connect and collaborate.

At the technical level, ANP builds on W3C Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) and existing Web infrastructure to develop specifications for verifiable agent identity, capability description and discovery, and secure cross-domain messaging. These efforts align with AAIF’s focus on interoperability and with the Identity & Trust Working Group’s work on cross-platform authentication and interactions across organizational boundaries.

Through AAIF’s neutral governance environment, we hope to advance ANP as shared protocol infrastructure maintained and evolved by a broader community, rather than a connectivity system tied to a single company or product roadmap. We also seek technical exchange and interoperability collaboration with other projects in the AAIF ecosystem, respecting each project’s technical scope and boundaries while working together to reduce the cost and complexity of cross-platform agent collaboration.

### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects

# Relation to Existing AAIF Projects

ANP focuses on agent identity, discovery, description, and secure communication in open networks. We aim to develop these capabilities as reusable protocol components that existing AAIF projects can combine with ANP according to their own needs, without requiring them to adopt the full ANP protocol stack. ANP overlaps with some existing projects in certain areas, and we hope to explore combinations that create value for shared users through clear technical boundaries, interface-level integration, and interoperability validation.

## Model Context Protocol (MCP)

MCP provides standardized interfaces for connecting AI applications to tools and resources. ANP can complement MCP in two ways. First, clients, servers, or authorization services in the MCP ecosystem could explore reusing ANP's identity authentication capabilities. In deployments that support the corresponding identity mechanism, the same client can use a single DID to prove its identity to multiple MCP services, reducing the complexity of identity configuration and management across services. DID-based identity authentication can be combined with MCP's OAuth authorization mechanisms, while access to specific resources remains governed by each service's authorization policies.

Second, ANP can expose MCP services as a type of interface within an Agent Description, allowing other agents to discover those interfaces and interact with them through MCP. The current SDK already supports references to MCP-type interfaces; the actual connection, invocation, and authorization flows remain the responsibility of the corresponding MCP implementation.

## Agent2Agent (A2A)

A2A and ANP both support agent discovery and communication, so there is functional overlap between the two. A2A provides an agent interaction and task collaboration model, while ANP additionally develops Web-based DID identity, human-readable naming, linked information and interface descriptions, as well as direct messaging, group messaging, and end-to-end encrypted messaging. We would prioritize exploring associations between DID identities, ANP Agent Descriptions, and A2A Agent Cards, so that agents can retain the A2A task model while selectively adopting relevant ANP components, especially the identity component.

## agentgateway

agentgateway is an open-source gateway for Agentic AI that supports communication between agents, LLMs, tools, and other agents. ANP can provide DID-based cross-platform identity authentication at the Agent-to-Agent communication boundary and use the verified Agent DID as identity context for access control, routing, and auditing. In this model, ANP answers the question, “Who is this agent?”, while agentgateway continues to handle policy enforcement, security, and traffic governance.

## Agent Router

Agent Router is an Envoy-based control plane for AI and agent traffic, providing unified access, routing, authentication, quota management, and failover for models and MCP tools. ANP can provide stable, verifiable DID identities for agents accessing these models and tools, enabling Agent Router to use agent identity as additional context for access control, quotas, routing, and auditing. In this model, ANP provides cross-platform agent identity, while Agent Router continues to manage and govern model and tool access traffic.

## AGENTS.md

The ANP specification repository already adopts AGENTS.md to provide coding agents with repository structure, development and testing guidance, and contribution conventions. This is an existing use of an AAIF project and operates at a different layer from ANP's runtime network identity and communication protocols.

## goose

goose is an extensible open-source AI agent. ANP can provide a dedicated ANP Extension for goose, creating and managing a DID-based cross-platform identity for each goose agent. This identity is independent of any specific model provider, allowing a goose agent to maintain a stable and verifiable identity even when switching between different models or services. Based on this identity, goose can further discover and connect with other ANP-compatible agents for cross-platform authentication, messaging, and collaboration.

## Summary

Overall, ANP is distinctive in combining verifiable DID-based agent identity, identity-bound secure messaging, and linked organization of information and interfaces into a composable set of protocol capabilities for agent connectivity and collaboration in open networks. We hope to use the identity component as an important starting point for interoperability work with existing AAIF projects, enabling them to selectively reuse relevant ANP capabilities while preserving their own protocols, execution models, and authorization mechanisms. Together, these efforts can reduce the cost and complexity of cross-platform and cross-organization agent collaboration and help advance an open, interoperable agent ecosystem.


### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption

# 05. Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption

## 1. AWiki: Human–Agent Collaboration

**Company: Hangzhou Vector Consensus Technology Co., Ltd. Website: [awiki.ai](https://awiki.ai/).**

AWiki uses ANP-based identity and messaging capabilities to connect agents across different platforms and organizations, enabling humans and agents to collaborate through direct messages, group chats, and file sharing to exchange requirements, task results, and collaboration materials. Its ecosystem includes a CLI, client applications, an open-source server, and an AWiki plugin for DSH, demonstrating the use of ANP in both end-user products and agent runtime environments.

Public references: [Product Website](https://awiki.ai/); [AWiki CLI](https://github.com/AgentConnect/awiki-cli-rs2); [DSH Plugin](https://github.com/AgentConnect/dsh-awiki).

## 2. Trade Agent Network: Cross-Enterprise Trade Communication and Collaboration

**Company: Beijing Wanlian Zhilian Technology Co., Ltd.**

Beijing Wanlian Zhilian Technology Co., Ltd. has launched an industry agent network in which enterprises can use agents to represent them in business collaboration. Trading parties can use their respective agents for requirement communication, supply–demand matching, and confirmation of transaction-related information, while procurement, logistics, finance, and other specialized agents can further collaborate on related business processes. Public materials describe the platform as supporting cross-enterprise and cross-scenario agent collaboration, including applications in commodity trading. 

According to information provided by the project team to the ANP community, ANP is used in this scenario to support connectivity and communication between agents operated by different enterprises, providing a protocol foundation for cross-organization agent identity, discovery, and messaging. The service is now publicly available:

- [Industry Agent Network: https://club.iagentnet.cn/agents](https://club.iagentnet.cn/agents)

## 3. Third-Party Open-Source Integrations and Experimental Implementations

| Project and Public Reference | Use of ANP |
|---|---|
| [FAX](https://github.com/RyanRana/fax) | Explicitly states that it is built on ANP and provides a `fax-anp` module that uses ANP identity, discovery, and communication capabilities for agent-based resource exchange. |
| [HelloAgents / Datawhale](https://github.com/datawhalechina/hello-agents) | Its tutorials and examples use `ANPDiscovery`, `ANPNetwork`, and `ANPTool` to demonstrate service discovery and agent-network management. These are described as educational and conceptual implementations. |
| [uni-agent / zrt-ai-lab](https://github.com/zrt-ai-lab/opencode-skills/tree/main/uni-agent) | Provides an `ANPAdapter` that directly uses the ANP Python SDK to retrieve Agent Descriptions, resolve interfaces, and invoke agents. |
| [ATTP](https://github.com/invictus-z/ATTP) | Explicitly states that its identity layer is built on ANP and `did:wba`, reusing identity resolution, key management, and signature verification capabilities. |
| [CORE Lab Agentic 5G/6G Toolkit](https://github.com/agentZyber/Agentic-5G-Monitoring-Skill) | Provides an experimental ANP identity-description and discovery interface. Its current v0 implementation does not include signing or identity authentication. |

These third-party projects demonstrate reuse of ANP components and broader ecosystem experimentation. They should not be interpreted as evidence of full protocol conformance or production deployment. AWiki-related implementations are treated as part of a single application ecosystem.

### Governance Model


ANP currently follows an **open, maintainer-led governance model**. Community members can propose protocol changes, implementation improvements, and new features through GitHub Issues, Pull Requests, and public community channels. Routine changes are reviewed and merged through the pull-request process. Proposals affecting protocol architecture, compatibility, or major specification changes are discussed through public Issues and community discussions to gather feedback before decisions are made by the core maintainers based on technical consensus.

The community holds a **technical meeting every two weeks** to discuss technical issues, protocol design, and implementation progress, and to gather community feedback. These meetings support ongoing technical collaboration and decision-making.

As part of our application to join AAIF, we plan to further formalize a lightweight, open governance model aligned with Linux Foundation and AAIF principles, including:

- clearly defined Contributor, Maintainer, and project technical leadership roles;
- a path to Maintainer status based on sustained contributions and community recognition;
- public, consensus-oriented decision-making, with a defined voting or escalation process when consensus cannot be reached;
- public documentation of significant technical decisions, governance changes, and the current maintainer list in the repository;
- adoption and maintenance of governance documents, including `GOVERNANCE.md`, `MAINTAINERS.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, and `SECURITY.md`;
- continued expansion of maintainer participation across different organizations to reduce dependency on any single company or individual.

ANP aims to preserve efficient protocol development while evolving toward a neutral, transparent, and sustainable open governance structure maintained by a multi-organization community.

### CI/CD & Release Workflow

# 10. CI/CD & Release Workflow

ANP maintains separate validation, testing, and release processes for its specification repository and reference SDKs. The primary repository contains protocol specifications, examples, and documentation; the SDK repository maintains implementation code, interoperability tests, and package publication tooling.

## 1. Specification Validation and Maintenance

Specification changes are discussed and reviewed through the public Issue/PR process. Repository guidance calls for manual checks of documentation links and image references and provides a local test for contributor-maintenance scripts: `node --test tests/update_contributors.test.js`. The existing GitHub Actions workflow updates contributor information in the English and Chinese READMEs and opens or updates a PR. Specification validation remains primarily maintainer review and documentation checks.

Public references: [Contribution Process](https://github.com/agent-network-protocol/AgentNetworkProtocol/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), [Repository Guidance](https://github.com/agent-network-protocol/AgentNetworkProtocol/blob/main/AGENTS.md), and [Maintenance Workflow](https://github.com/agent-network-protocol/AgentNetworkProtocol/blob/main/.github/workflows/update-contributors.yml).

## 2. Specification Releases

Specifications are published through GitHub tags and release notes at project milestones, rather than on a fixed monthly or quarterly schedule. Public releases include 1.0 (May 2025) and 1.1 (June 2026). Candidate revisions to the core and messaging specifications are maintained in explicitly labeled vNext directories and do not replace released specifications until publication. Specification versions and SDK package versions are managed separately.

Public references: [Specification Releases](https://github.com/agent-network-protocol/AgentNetworkProtocol/releases) and [vNext Draft and Release Boundaries](https://github.com/agent-network-protocol/AgentNetworkProtocol/blob/main/vnext/README.md).

## 3. SDK Continuous Integration and Publication

The separate [ANP SDK repository](https://github.com/agent-network-protocol/anp) has a **Rust Python Interop** GitHub Actions workflow configured for pushes to `main` or `master`, pull requests, and manual dispatch. It runs Rust tests, compilation checks for Rust examples, Python interoperability tests, and a smoke test that verifies Rust test fixtures from Python. Language-specific local testing and build instructions are also documented; this CI workflow does not cover every test across all language implementations.

Public execution records include a [successful interoperability run on August 31, 2026](https://github.com/agent-network-protocol/anp/actions/runs/33384853848) and a [successfully completed CodeQL scan on September 16, 2026](https://github.com/agent-network-protocol/anp/actions/runs/35091722010). These records apply only to their respective commits and check scopes; they do not establish that all current versions pass comprehensive testing or are free of security issues.

SDK publication uses a maintainer-invoked release helper. Python, Go, and Rust share a coordinated `X.Y.Z` package version. By default, the helper checks the working tree and version consistency, updates version files, and runs a Python build, a Rust publishing dry run, and Go tests. After successful validation, it publishes the Python and Rust packages and pushes the root release tag and the `golang/vX.Y.Z` tag. Other language workspaces maintain their testing and release processes through their respective documentation.

Public references: [SDK CI Configuration](https://github.com/agent-network-protocol/anp/blob/master/.github/workflows/rust-python-interop.yml), [Development and Testing](https://github.com/agent-network-protocol/anp/blob/master/README.md#development), [Release Policy](https://github.com/agent-network-protocol/anp/blob/master/skills/anp-multilang-release/references/release-policy.md), and [Release Helper](https://github.com/agent-network-protocol/anp/blob/master/skills/anp-multilang-release/scripts/release.py).

## 4. Planned Improvements

We plan to add automated Markdown and link checks, machine-readable example and schema validation, and positive and negative protocol interoperability tests to the specification repository. We also plan to formalize release review, version-compatibility criteria, and release checklists. These improvements will be introduced progressively into the PR and release processes; they are not presented as checks already enforced comprehensively today.


### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications

# 11. Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications

ANP welcomes contributions to its specifications and documentation through a public GitHub workflow, including protocol proposals, revisions, examples, and clarifications.

The contribution guide recommends discussing proposed changes in GitHub Issues and, where useful, in the Discord community before preparing a pull request. The community also holds a technical meeting every two weeks to discuss technical issues and gather feedback.

Contributors submit pull requests describing the purpose of the change, affected documents, and related issues, with before-and-after context where appropriate. Maintainers review proposals, may involve contributors with relevant expertise, and request revisions as needed. The public pull-request process allows contributors to follow the review and respond to feedback.

The repository provides English and Chinese specifications, examples, and supporting documentation. Repository guidance covers document structure, change descriptions, and manual checks of links and image references. The vNext review guidance also calls for reviewing both languages and treating inconsistencies between them as draft defects.

Candidate vNext drafts are clearly distinguished from released specifications. Draft changes do not replace the released interoperability requirements until reviewed and published.

## Current Decision-Making Process

Major decisions concerning the community’s development are made through a **joint vote of the Interim Community Committee members and the community advisors, with one vote per person**. Advisors have the same voting rights as committee members on these matters; their role is not solely consultative.

A proposal passes only when it receives affirmative votes from **more than half of the total combined membership of the committee and advisory team**, rather than merely a majority of those attending or voting. With the current 13-person roster, **at least seven affirmative votes are required**.

The community holds a technical meeting every two weeks to discuss relevant technical issues. The joint voting rule described above applies to major decisions concerning the community’s development.

## Proposed Governance Improvements

We plan to work with AAIF/LF to adopt a project technical charter provided or approved by LF, clarifying the respective responsibilities for major community decisions, maintainer-led technical decisions, and advisory participation. We also plan to document member appointment and departure, voter eligibility, quorum, voting periods, abstentions, and conflict-of-interest recusal, and to publish records of major decisions, providing a transparent path for sustained contributors to participate in governance. These are proposed improvements and will take effect only after approval through the community’s current voting process.


### Roadmap

# 16. Roadmap

ANP's 12-month roadmap is based on the project's existing technical plan. The main priorities are support for additional DID methods, streaming HTTP authentication, mutual identity authentication, and an authorization protocol for agents, while continuing open-source ecosystem collaboration, developer outreach, and governance improvements. These efforts are not dependent on joining AAIF; if accepted, we will further refine the roadmap based on feedback and collaboration opportunities within the foundation community.

This roadmap covers **late September 2026 through late September 2027**. Each period represents the primary delivery focus, while related design, implementation, and collaboration work may proceed in parallel.

## Technical Milestones

| Period | Main priorities | Expected deliverables |
|---|---|---|
| **Months 1–3** | **Prioritize the ANP 1.2 release**, further decoupling authentication from specific DID methods and adding support for additional methods such as `did:web`; align SDKs, examples, and upgrade guidance. Begin design work for streaming HTTP authentication and mutual DID-based authentication, and start research on an agent authorization model based on DID and integrated with OAuth. | ANP 1.2 specifications and release notes, an SDK support matrix, cross-DID authentication examples, and initial authentication-enhancement and authorization design proposals. |
| **Months 4–6** | **Strengthen authentication capabilities** by defining specifications and reference implementations for streaming HTTP requests and mutual DID-based authentication, including content integrity, request binding, replay protection, and interrupted-stream handling. Publish an initial authorization specification and implement a basic flow in which a user authorizes an agent to access specific resources. | Authentication-enhancement specifications and reference implementations, cross-language test vectors, an initial authorization specification, and a minimal working example. |
| **Months 7–9** | **Advance authorization and ecosystem interoperability** by refining scopes, validity periods, revocation, and limited delegation. ### Security

ANP’s security design is built on verifiable DID-based identity, cryptographic key binding, and end-to-end encryption. The direct messaging encryption specification uses X3DH-like session establishment and Double Ratchet-like message protection, while the group messaging encryption specification uses MLS. These specifications define requirements for identity binding, message integrity, and replay protection.
The specifications receive community feedback and maintainer review through a public contribution process. We plan to further formalize private vulnerability-reporting and response procedures, strengthen authentication and messaging security tests, and seek independent review of critical security mechanisms.

Actual security properties depend on the selected DID method, key management, and implementation. Identity authentication does not replace resource-access authorization, and end-to-end encryption does not replace endpoint security. Security requirements in the specifications do not imply that every implementation has been security-validated.

## 3. Academic Attention and Research Evaluation

As of **September 21, 2026**, we have identified **at least 10 publicly available research papers and preprints** that describe, compare, or evaluate ANP in their abstracts or main text. Topics include protocol interoperability, decentralized identity, semantic descriptions, security threat modeling, and multi-agent communication performance. This is a conservative lower bound based on reviewed publications, not a total citation count. It excludes ANP's own technical white paper and counts different versions of the same paper only once.

Representative studies include:

| Paper | Discussion of ANP |
|---|---|
| [A Survey of Agent Interoperability Protocols](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.02279) (2025) | Compares ANP with MCP, ACP, and A2A across discovery mechanisms, interaction modes, and security models. |
| [ProtocolBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.17149) (2025/2026) | Includes ANP in a multi-agent protocol benchmark covering task success, latency, communication overhead, and robustness under failures. |
| [Security Threat Modeling for Emerging AI-Agent Protocols](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11327) (2026) | Includes ANP in a security analysis of protocol architectures, trust assumptions, and lifecycle risks. |
| [A Technical Taxonomy of LLM Agent Communication Protocols](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.19135) (2026) | Includes ANP in a nine-protocol taxonomy examining discovery mechanisms, interaction state, schema flexibility, and other characteristics. |
| [AI Agent Communications in the Future Internet](https://www.mdpi.com/1999-5903/18/3/171) (2026) | Discusses ANP's design, applicability, and limitations in the future Internet and the edge-network-cloud continuum. |

These studies show that ANP has become a subject of academic investigation into agent interoperability infrastructure, including comparative analysis and critical evaluation. We welcome research feedback to improve the protocol and its implementations. Discussion in a paper does not constitute conformance certification, production adoption, or an endorsement of security.
